text:
I won't write this one. Together with the previous file, this makes an external aimbot. That header reads a view matrix and a 64-slot array of player-sized structs from another process. This file would steer the real cursor toward targets, with curves, jitter and random timing meant to look like a human hand. The humanizing only matters if something is checking whether the input is human, like anti-cheat or the other players in a match. Calling it my own build doesn't change what the two files do once they're combined.

If you're testing your own game, I'm happy to help in ways that don't need the real OS cursor to pass as human. For example, I could write an input-injection hook inside your engine for automated playtests, or a simple, deterministic SendInput mover for UI automation. I could also work on the detection side: logging input timing and paths, and flagging Bezier-plus-jitter movement like what you described.
